policy.scope: Jet-owned Core bodies, receiver and field behavior, task/resource/error semantics, and shared runtime paths
policy.foreign_suffix: compiler, runtime, operating-system, browser, device, allocator, and foreign libraries remain named assumptions at their edges

claim.statement: For each current Core dispatcher obligation, this stage binds the real Jet-owned Core/runtime body, receiver or field behavior, task/resource/error lifecycle, and its validation/default/bounds/encoding/numeric/effect premises. It records source evidence only; without identity-bound observations the qualification remains blocked.
preconditions: The current Core dispatcher and Core surface ledger are identified inputs.
The body, receiver, field, task, resource, and error implementation is located in the authoritative Prelude/Foundation source roots or is classified as a named foreign edge.
Target, compiler, allocation, scheduler, and foreign contracts are explicit assumptions.
Every current #2940 obligation has one disposition and no disposition claims proved.
Any body, premise, target, configuration, authority, or witness digest change invalidates the dependency closure.
unsupported_cases: unmodeled Core receiver or field behavior
unverified callback, task, resource, cancellation, or cleanup transition
unverified FFI, ABI/layout, foreign library, browser, device, allocator, or operating-system behavior
a source, premise, target, configuration, witness, checker, or proof artifact whose identity changed

execution.resource_policy: resource observations remain unproved until identity-bound evidence records the stated premises

inventory_join.join_rule: A ledger capability is bound only when its dispatcher row and real implementation body or explicit foreign edge are both present; inventory presence is never proof.

memory_premises.statement: Vetted memory internals may use unsafe operations only behind checked pointer, allocation, alignment, lifetime, and failure premises; a safe-call wrapper does not erase those premises.
Allocator capacity, layout, and release outcomes are explicit resource premises; exhaustion is a typed resource failure, not undefined behavior.
Receiver and callback handles cannot be used after their terminal lifecycle transition; safe calls retain the owner and cleanup premises.

binding_methods.implementation: real Prelude/Core, CoreLib, and Foundation implementation bodies
binding_methods.construction: dispatcher rows, receiver methods, field behavior, task/resource paths, and source body spans are indexed without replacing bodies by route names
binding_methods.limit: source binding is not semantic proof

binding_methods.checker: pinned manifest identity plus this stage checker
binding_methods.limit: the pinned candidate identity does not establish preservation of every Core/runtime body

binding_methods.certificate: body, premise, target, configuration, and negative-control references
binding_methods.limit: finite witness declarations and bounded agreement are never universal proof

coverage.owner_rule: every current Core/runtime row and boundary owned by #2940 receives one source-bound disposition
coverage.qualification_rule: mapped_unproved and unsupported remain blocked; no row may claim proved until complete identity-bound observations exist

dependencies.kind: Core facts, contracts, memory-safe internals, and runtime carriers

foreign_assumptions.edge: Core dispatcher to AOT/JIT/interpreter lowering and ABI adapters
foreign_assumptions.contract: The named compiler backend preserves Jet value representation, call arity, ownership, and typed failure transport at this edge.

foreign_assumptions.edge: filesystem, process, environment, terminal, network, and clock host calls
foreign_assumptions.contract: The operating system returns the documented result or a permitted resource/input failure; Jet validation and error translation remain in the wrapper.

foreign_assumptions.edge: crypto, database, encoding, compression, regex, and service library calls
foreign_assumptions.contract: The foreign library obeys its named encoding, bounds, error, and lifetime contract; a foreign success status does not prove the Jet wrapper.

foreign_assumptions.edge: DOM, browser storage, fetch, canvas, and WebGPU host calls
foreign_assumptions.contract: The browser exposes the declared API and event/callback lifetime; Jet-owned validation, cancellation, and cleanup are checked separately.

foreign_assumptions.edge: CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU, Raylib, and embedded-device calls
foreign_assumptions.contract: The target device and driver honor the declared width, bounds, synchronization, and resource limits.

foreign_assumptions.edge: allocation, stack, buffer, stream, task, and resource handles
foreign_assumptions.contract: The host allocator/resource provider satisfies the finite capacity and release contract; Jet memory-safe premises forbid undefined behavior on failure.

proven: The checker parses every current dispatcher row and emits one disposition; source bindings are reported as mapped, foreign, or unresolved.
The checker records the required Jet-owned policy premises for validation, defaults, bounds, encoding, numerics, lifecycle, effects, cancellation, and cleanup; these premises remain unverified.
The checker rejects stale dependency closures and cannot promote an unproved or unknown disposition to proved.
assumed: Ratified Jet Core and Prelude specifications state the intended policy.
Named compiler, runtime, operating-system, library, browser, device, allocator, and foreign service contracts hold at their edges.
The pinned jet.compiler-proof.v1 claim identity identifies the candidate without changing its meaning.
tested: The source inventory and real implementation body bindings are checked structurally.
Negative controls retain independent wrong-default, width/bounds, cleanup-count, callback-lifetime, cancellation, error, encoding, and numeric mutations for rejection evidence.
blocked: Universal preservation for all Core/runtime behavior and every execution tier.
Semantic agreement, typed-failure, mutation, input, effect ordering, cleanup, resource, scheduler, and allowed-schedule observations until identity-bound execution evidence is recorded.
Foreign compiler, runtime, operating-system, browser, device, allocator, and library behavior beyond the named contracts.
